sentences.zh: 世界上大部分地区对进口石油的依赖甚至更深，面对伊拉克的威胁也更加脆弱。

sentences.en: Because suddenly, those foreign sources of oil that we still needed, because we weren't quite energy independent, they were at risk of being overtaken by Saddam Hussein.
sentences.zh: 因为突然之间，我们仍然需要的那些外国石油来源——由于我们尚未完全实现能源独立——面临着被萨达姆·侯赛因吞并的风险。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So all of those things were done.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些措施都采取了。

sentences.en: But all that was accomplished, and it was something, was to stem the bleeding.
sentences.zh: 但所有这些成就——也确实取得了一些成就——不过是止血而已。

sentences.en: And that brings us to the second trauma, which is the early years of the current century.
sentences.zh: 这就把我们带到了第二场创伤，也就是本世纪的头几年。

sentences.en: When suddenly our production is in decline again,
sentences.zh: 当时我们的产量突然再次下降，

sentences.en: China is growing by leaps and bounds.
sentences.zh: 中国正在突飞猛进地增长。

sentences.en: India is starting to grow by leaps and bounds.
sentences.zh: 印度也开始突飞猛进地增长。

sentences.en: A middle class is growing around the developing world.
sentences.zh: 整个发展中世界的中产阶级正在壮大。

sentences.en: So demand is going up like 5 million barrels a day around the world.
sentences.zh: 因此全球需求每天都在增加大约500万桶。

sentences.en: And the Middle East is suddenly more unstable.
sentences.zh: 而中东突然变得更加动荡。

sentences.en: And so prices skyrocket between the years of about 2004 and 2007.
sentences.zh: 所以在2004年到2007年左右，价格飙升。

sentences.en: And when you say skyrocketing, what do you mean?
sentences.zh: 当你说道价格飙升时，具体指什么？

sentences.en: I mean prices skyrocket to as high as $147 a barrel.
sentences.zh: 我是指油价飙升到了每桶147美元的高位。

sentences.en: Correct me if I'm wrong, this is the point where U.S.
sentences.zh: 如果我没记错的话，这就是美国

sentences.en: gasoline prices at the pump reach $5 a gallon.
sentences.zh: 加油站的汽油价格达到每加仑5美元的时候。

sentences.en: And I remember how upsetting that was to consumers and to voters.
sentences.zh: 我记得这对消费者和选民来说是多么令人沮丧。

sentences.en: Yes, it was very, very upsetting.
sentences.zh: 是的，非常非常沮丧。

sentences.en: And for those of a certain age, it was a reminder of the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 对一定年龄的人来说，这勾起了对20世纪70年代的回忆。

sentences.en: We were right back in the same problem, dependent on foreign oil, which was very expensive.
sentences.zh: 我们又回到了老问题上，依然依赖价格高昂的外国石油。

sentences.en: But then something big happened.
sentences.zh: 但随后发生了大事。

sentences.en: There was a Texas oil man named George Mitchell.
sentences.zh: 有个名叫乔治·米切尔的德克萨斯石油商人。

sentences.en: And for years and years, he had been experimenting with hydraulic fracturing,
sentences.zh: 多年来，他一直在试验水力压裂技术，

sentences.en: which is basically splitting up shale, hard shale rock, which had been useless when drilled vertically.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是将页岩（坚硬的页岩岩石）裂开，这种岩石在垂直钻井时曾毫无用处。

sentences.en: George Mitchell came up with the idea of drilling horizontally through these layers of rock and unleashing the oil in the rock by basically exploding the rock
sentences.zh: 乔治·米切尔想出了一个主意：通过这些岩层进行水平钻探，基本上是通过炸裂岩石来释放岩石中的石油，

sentences.en: and then introducing sand and water to keep the cracks open, releasing the oil.
sentences.zh: 然后注入沙子和水来保持裂缝张开，从而释放石油。

sentences.en: Fracking.
sentences.zh: 压裂法。

sentences.en: Fracking.
sentences.zh: 压裂法。

sentences.en: Consider this a eureka moment for the rest of the world.
sentences.zh: 这对世界其他地方来说无异于一个灵光乍现的时刻。

sentences.en: The biggest energy innovation of the decade.
sentences.zh: 这是这十年里最大的能源创新。

sentences.en: Suddenly, they were able to release enormous amounts of oil in fields that big companies had given up on years before.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，他们能够释放出大公司几年前已经放弃的油田中的巨量石油。

sentences.en: The so-called shale revolution has spawned boom towns in the Dakotas.
sentences.zh: 所谓的页岩革命在达科他州催生了一座座因石油繁荣的城镇。

sentences.en: That's a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 那是大笔的钱。

sentences.en: It's life-changing money.
sentences.zh: 这是能改变人生命运的财富。

sentences.en: It's a dream.
sentences.zh: 这是一个梦想。

sentences.en: We were able to do it in North Dakota, Texas, Colorado, Oklahoma, a few other places.
sentences.zh: 我们得以在北达科他州、德克萨斯州、科罗拉多州、俄克拉荷马州以及其他一些地方做到这一点。

sentences.en: Thanks to fracking technology, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 多亏了压裂技术，美国

sentences.en: now producing about 9.5 million barrels a day, a 70% jump from just five years ago.
sentences.zh: 现在的产量约为每天950万桶，比仅仅五年前暴增了70%。

sentences.en: And it's occurring because the price of oil was so high.
sentences.zh: 这一切的发生是因为油价曾如此高昂。

sentences.en: That incentivized innovation.
sentences.zh: 这刺激了创新。

sentences.en: And Cliff, what does fracking for oil mean for this still quite unfinished American dream of energy independence?
sentences.zh: 克利夫，开采石油的压裂技术，对于美国至今尚未完全实现的能源独立梦想意味着什么？

sentences.en: Well, it means that we actually, at least momentarily, seem to almost reach that independence
sentences.zh: 嗯，这意味着我们实际上，至少在暂时看来，似乎几乎实现了这种独立，

sentences.en: because American oil production more than doubled in about five years.
sentences.zh: 因为美国的石油产量在大约五年内翻了一番多。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Last year, we relied less on foreign oil than in any of the last 16 years.
sentences.zh: 去年，我们对外国石油的依赖程度创下了过去16年来的最低纪录。

sentences.en: It's changed the whole world and the economy of the whole world.
sentences.zh: 它改变了整个世界以及全球经济。

sentences.en: It's changed our dependence on foreign oil.
sentences.zh: 它改变了我们对外国石油的依赖。

sentences.en: It's changed our alliances in terms of their value to us.
sentences.zh: 它改变了我们对各种盟友价值的看法。

sentences.en: The United States became an exporter of oil for the first time in many years.
sentences.zh: 多年来美国首次成为了石油出口国。

sentences.en: And last year, actually leapfrogged over Russia and Saudi Arabia as the biggest oil producer in the world.
sentences.zh: 而且去年，美国实际上超越了俄罗斯和沙特阿拉伯，成为了世界上最大的产油国。

sentences.en: So this seems like a pretty good problem to have, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这似乎是一个相当不错的“烦恼”，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, too much American oil for the first time, basically, in our history.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，基本上在我们历史上首次出现了美国石油过剩。

sentences.en: Economically speaking, no question about it.
sentences.zh: 从经济角度来说，毫无疑问。

sentences.en: By 2014, we were bringing down gasoline prices for consumers.
sentences.zh: 到2014年，我们一直在为消费者拉低汽油价格。

sentences.en: It was part of our recovery from the recession.
sentences.zh: 这是我们从经济衰退中复苏的一部分。

sentences.en: And all of this American production puts the United States in an extremely powerful position economically,
sentences.zh: 所有这些美国本土产量把美国推到了经济上极其强大的地位，

sentences.en: employing millions of people and producing revenues for state and local governments across much of the country,
sentences.zh: 为数百万人提供了就业岗位，并为全国许多地方的州和地方政府创造了财政收入，

sentences.en: also giving the United States the freedom to act in foreign policy in ways that would have been unheard of years before,
sentences.zh: 同时也赋予了美国在外交政策上采取前所未有的行动的自由，

sentences.en: such as putting pressure on Iran without endangering our energy supply.
sentences.zh: 比如在不危及我们能源供应的情况下对伊朗施压。

sentences.en: It was basically the culmination of the dream from the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是20世纪70年代梦想的顶峰。

sentences.en: And it was hard to imagine just a few months ago what could happen that could undercut that dream.
sentences.zh: 就在几个月前，人们还很难想象会发生什么来破坏这个梦想。

sentences.en: Like a pandemic.
sentences.zh: 比如一场大流行病。

sentences.en: Like a pandemic that would suddenly destroy the demand for oil and kneecap the American oil industry that had produced all of this oil in the first place.
sentences.zh: 比如一场会突然摧毁石油需求的大流行病，并给原本生产了所有这些石油的美国石油工业当头棒喝。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 已解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你能免费探索《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间可以突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用，享受30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So Cliff, when this third trauma arrives, the pandemic, the world at this point, and the United States in particular, is awash in oil.
sentences.zh: 所以克利夫，当这第三场创伤到来时——这场大流行病，此时的世界，尤其是美国，正充斥着过剩的石油。

sentences.en: And from what you're saying, demand for that oil has instantly plunged.
sentences.zh: 从你的话来看，对这些石油的需求瞬间暴跌了。

sentences.en: So what's actually happening to all of this overproduced oil?
sentences.zh: 那么所有这些过剩生产的石油到底怎么样了？

sentences.en: So the oil has no place to go, and it's rapidly filling up tank farms, strategic reserves around the world.
sentences.zh: 所以石油无处可去，它正迅速填满全球各地的罐区和战略储备。

sentences.en: Refineries are running out of space to put the oil.
sentences.zh: 炼油厂存放石油的空间已经告急。

sentences.en: And so the inventories are building to a point where there'll be no physical space to put the oil.
sentences.zh: 因此库存不断增加，直到存放石油的物理空间不复存在。

sentences.en: You now have tankers, which used to ship oil from place to place, just storing the oil and sitting out off of the shores of Los Angeles, for instance, and other places.
sentences.zh: 你现在可以看到那些以前用于在各地运送石油的油轮，如今只是用来储存石油，停泊在洛杉矶等地的海岸附近。

sentences.en: And these are the people who are making a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 而正是这群人正在赚大钱。

sentences.en: They're getting paid to just hold the oil.
sentences.zh: 他们光是保管石油就能拿到报酬。

sentences.en: So this explains those negative oil prices, right?
sentences.zh: 这就解释了那些负油价现象，对吧？

sentences.en: They're producing so much oil that they have nowhere to store it, so they end up having to pay people to take it.
sentences.zh: 他们生产的石油实在太多，以至于无处储存，最后不得不付钱让人拿走。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 一点没错。

sentences.en: Cliff, maybe this is a bit of a stupid question, but why don't oil producers, knowing that there's just way too much oil,
sentences.zh: 克利夫，这或许是个有点愚蠢的问题，但石油生产商既然知道石油实在太多，

sentences.en: and that if they keep producing it, they're going to hurt their own ability to command meaningful prices, just stop pumping or fracking oil?
sentences.zh: 而且如果继续生产，就会损害他们自身获取可观价格的能力，为什么不干脆停止开采或压裂石油呢？

sentences.en: Just leave it in the ground.
sentences.zh: 干脆把它留在地底。

sentences.en: Well, that's beginning to happen, but it's a cumbersome, complex process.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这种情况开始发生了，但这是一个繁琐而复杂的的过程。

sentences.en: First of all, you have thousands of producers in the United States.
sentences.zh: 首先，美国有数千家生产商。

sentences.en: We don't have a national oil company which is taking orders from the government, such as in Saudi Arabia.
sentences.zh: 我们没有像沙特阿拉伯那样听从政府指令的国家石油公司。

sentences.en: And then there are complications that go along with shutting in wells.
sentences.zh: 其次，关闭油井还伴随着各种复杂情况。

sentences.en: It's an expensive process.
sentences.zh: 这是一个昂贵的过程。

sentences.en: You can actually damage the resource to the point where when you restart the oil, you'll actually pump less oil out.
sentences.zh: 你甚至可能会破坏油气资源，以至于当你重新开采时，抽出的石油反而会变少。

sentences.en: And then you have all of these companies that even when they're losing money, they need cash flow.
sentences.zh: 此外，所有这些公司即使在亏损时也需要现金流。

sentences.en: They need cash flow to meet their payroll, to meet their debt responsibilities.
sentences.zh: 他们需要现金流来支付工资和偿还债务。

sentences.en: So what oil companies prefer to do, you let the well basically slowly decline.
sentences.zh: 所以石油公司更倾向于这样做：让油井的产量基本上缓慢下降。

sentences.en: So if we can't easily turn off the pumps and we can't suddenly overnight create enough storage for all this oil, what can and I guess what is the U.S.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果我们无法轻易关闭油泵，也无法在一夜之间突然为所有这些石油创造足够的储存空间，那么美国能够——我想它也正在——

sentences.en: doing about this glut of oil?
sentences.zh: 针对石油过剩采取什么行动？

sentences.en: Well, there are a number of things that are being considered, such as stopping imports from coming in, particularly imports from Saudi Arabia that are on their way in tankers.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有许多正在考虑的措施，比如叫停进口，尤其是那些正在用油轮运往美国的沙特进口石油。

sentences.en: 40 million barrels of Saudi oil is already on its way to the United States.
sentences.zh: 4000万桶沙特石油已经运往美国途中。

sentences.en: But there are probably American refiners who have already paid for it.
sentences.zh: 但可能有一些美国炼油商已经为此付过钱了。

sentences.en: President Trump is facing pressure to stop Saudi crude oil imports in an effort to save the American oil industry.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统正面临压力，要求叫停沙特原油进口，以此来拯救美国石油工业。

sentences.en: And so you would be hurting American refiners.
sentences.zh: 这样一来就会伤害到美国炼油商。

sentences.en: That's not something that the administration would like to do, I'm sure.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定，这不是政府愿意做的事。

sentences.en: So they don't have a lot of options.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的选择并不多。

sentences.en: But meanwhile, small oil producers are in dire straits and on the verge of bankruptcy.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，小型石油生产商正处于水深火热之中，濒临破产。

sentences.en: And that could be the future, especially if our demand is going to be depressed for a long time.
sentences.zh: 这可能就是未来，特别是如果我们的需求长期低迷的话。

sentences.en: So Cliff, how is this new reality of the glut and the small producers struggling within that glut?
sentences.zh: 那么克利夫，这种石油过剩的新现实，以及小生产商在过剩中挣扎的局面，

sentences.en: How is that starting to look on the ground in America's biggest oil towns, including, I'm sure, yours, which is in Texas?
sentences.zh: 在美国最大的几个石油城镇（其中肯定包括你所在的德州）的实地情况开始是什么样的？

sentences.en: Well, thousands of people are losing their jobs.
sentences.zh: 嗯，成千上万的人正在失业。

sentences.en: Others are being furloughed.
sentences.zh: 其他人则在休无薪假。

sentences.en: And probably it's only going to get worse.
sentences.zh: 而且情况可能只会变得更糟。

sentences.en: You have oil states that rely on what's called severance taxes, which is dependent on the price of oil.
sentences.zh: 有些产油州依赖所谓的“离职税”（译注：指severance tax，即矿产资源开采税），这取决于油价。

sentences.en: So that will have an impact on state and local services.
sentences.zh: 所以这将会对州和地方服务产生影响。

sentences.en: And it'll have an impact on people who actually earn money because oil is coming out of fields on their private property.
sentences.zh: 它也会影响那些因为石油从自己私有土地上的油田开采出来而实际获得收入的人。

sentences.en: So there's going to be a big macroeconomic impact in these oil-producing states.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些产油州将受到巨大的宏观经济冲击。

sentences.en: Cliff,
sentences.zh: 克利夫，

sentences.en: there are going to be people who hear this and think this is what happens when a country like the United States becomes overly focused in this discussion of energy independence on old line forms of energy,
sentences.zh: 有些人听到这里会认为，这就是当像美国这样的国家在探讨能源独立时，过度聚焦于传统形式的能源、

sentences.en: on oil.
sentences.zh: 即石油时所发生的情况。

sentences.en: Well, rather than on newer, greener forms of energy.
sentences.zh: 而不是聚焦于更新、更环保的能源形式。

sentences.en: What do you say to that?
sentences.zh: 你对此怎么看？

sentences.en: So there are definitely going to be a lot of people who will celebrate the demise of the American oil industry.
sentences.zh: 所以肯定会有很多人庆祝美国石油工业的消亡。

sentences.en: And there is a strong argument to be made that we need to diversify our energy supply.
sentences.zh: 而且确实有一个强有力的论点：我们需要使能源供应多样化。

sentences.en: And we have done that successfully when it comes to power.
sentences.zh: 在电力方面，我们已经成功做到了这一点。

sentences.en: We are now using wind and solar, but not for our cars.
sentences.zh: 我们现在正在使用风能和太阳能，但我们的汽车不用。

sentences.en: The electrical age, the electric cars, they're coming.
sentences.zh: 电气化时代，电动汽车，它们正在到来。

sentences.en: There's no question about it.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问。

sentences.en: But it's going to take decades because the average car today is on the road for 10 years.
sentences.zh: 但这需要几十年时间，因为当今普通汽车的寿命是10年。

sentences.en: So it takes a long time to change the transportation fleet.
sentences.zh: 因此，改变交通运输车队需要很长时间。

sentences.en: And our transportation fleet is overwhelmingly dependent on gasoline and diesel.
sentences.zh: 而我们的交通运输车队绝大多数都依赖汽油和柴油。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Which comes, of course, from oil.
sentences.zh: 而它们当然都来自石油。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 一点没错。

sentences.en: Cliff,
sentences.zh: 克利夫，

sentences.en: what's so interesting about the history that you have described here is that it feels like every decision the United States has made about oil was about avoiding a single scenario,
sentences.zh: 你在这里描述的历史最有趣的地方在于，感觉美国关于石油做出的每一个决定，都是为了避免单一的情景，

sentences.en: which is that we would run out of oil.
sentences.zh: 那就是我们的石油会耗尽。

sentences.en: And we would be beholden to our adversaries to get that oil.
sentences.zh: 而且我们需要仰仗我们的对手来获取那些石油。

sentences.en: And it feels like we never really prepared for the opposite scenario, which is the situation we're in now.
sentences.zh: 而且感觉我们从未真正为相反的情况做过准备，也就是我们现在所处的这种局面。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Nobody anticipated a pandemic that would destroy demand.
sentences.zh: 没有人预料到会有摧毁需求的疫情。

sentences.en: And no one is to blame for this, but we are now facing an entirely new set of probleMs.
sentences.zh: 没有人应该为此受到指责，但我们现在面临着一套全新的一系列问题。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And, of course, if we had anticipated this problem, we would not have solved the problem that we had being dependent on producers in the Middle East and other unfriendly powers.
sentences.zh: 而且，当然，如果我们预料到了这个问题，我们就不会解决那种依赖中东和其他不友好势力的生产国的问题。

sentences.en: So my big takeaway, and it may be obvious to everyone, is the idea of energy security is simply an illusion.
sentences.zh: 所以我的最大感悟，可能对每个人来说都很明显，那就是能源安全的理念简直是个幻觉。

sentences.en: We are not energy secure when we have little oil and we're not energy secure when we have a lot of oil.
sentences.zh: 当我们石油很少时，我们没有能源安全；当我们石油很多时，我们也没有能源安全。

sentences.en: It's hard to get it just right.
sentences.zh: 要拿捏得恰到好处很难。

sentences.en: Thank you, Cliff.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，克利夫。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的内容。

sentences.en: On Sunday, the head of the White House Task Force on the Coronavirus, Dr. Deborah Birx, said that social distancing rules would likely remain in place throughout the summer,
sentences.zh: 周日，白宫冠状病毒工作组负责人黛博拉·比尔克斯博士表示，社交距离准则可能会在整个夏天保持有效，

sentences.en: even as some states begin reopening their economies.
sentences.zh: 尽管一些州开始重新开放经济。

sentences.en: During an interview on NBC's Meet the Press,
sentences.zh: 在接受全国广播公司《与媒体见面》节目采访时，

sentences.en: Birx was asked about President Trump's unproven claim made last week that an injection of a disinfectant like bleach could combat the virus.
sentences.zh: 比尔克斯被问及总统特朗普上周未经证实的言论，即注射消毒剂（如漂白剂）可以对抗病毒。

sentences.en: Dr. Birx, help me understand what happened with the suggestion that the president made that the task force study disinfected injection.
sentences.zh: 比尔克斯博士，请帮我理解一下，总统提出让工作组研究注射消毒剂的建议是怎么回事。

sentences.en: Do you have any more information and are you concerned that people might take bleach because of what the president said?
sentences.zh: 您还有更多信息吗？您是否担心人们会因为总统所说的话而去服用漂白剂？

sentences.en: I think I made it very clear and so has Dr. Fauci and everyone associated with the task force and their clarity around this is not a treatment.
sentences.zh: 我想我已经说得很清楚了，福奇博士以及所有与工作组相关的人也是如此，他们在这一点上的明确表态是：这不是一种治疗方法。

sentences.en: The president's statement was widely condemned and prompted local health officials and the makers of cleaning supplies to warn Americans not to ingest or inject their products.
sentences.zh: 总统的言论受到了广泛谴责，并促使地方卫生官员和清洁用品制造商警告美国人不要吞服或注射他们的产品。

sentences.en: As of Sunday night, the coronavirus had infected more than 938,000 Americans and has killed at least 50,000 of them.
sentences.zh: 截至周日晚间，冠状病毒已感染了超过93.8万美国人，并造成至少5万人死亡。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine until this summer when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器在运作，直到今年夏天选举迎来了许多自称改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场残酷、混乱且有时令人激动的争斗之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在由我萨拉·科尼格主持的最新一期《都市》节目中，讲述了人们试图保持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《都市》。

sentences.zh: 请在你获取播客的任何地方收听。
